hooks.text: A dormant supermassive black hole fired a particle jet directly at Earth.
A dormant black hole woke up and aimed a relativistic jet at Earth.
A blinding beam traveled 3.8 billion light-years aimed straight at Earth.

title: The Black Hole Jet Pointed at Earth
description: When a dormant supermassive black hole shredded a star 3.8 billion light-years away, its relativistic jet pointed directly at Earth.

beats.text: Most cosmic blasts fade within seconds, but NASA's Swift satellite detected a source that flared repeatedly with intense X-rays for days.
beats.visual: artist's concept of the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory in Earth orbit, 2004

beats.text: In the northern constellation Draco, an approaching star was gravitationally ripped completely to shreds.

beats.text: The shredder was a dormant supermassive black hole lurking inside the core of a distant galaxy.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope optical view of a distant host galaxy core, 2011
queries: Hubble Space Telescope distant galaxy core

beats.text: As stellar debris fell into an accretion disk, it launched a particle jet traveling near the speed of light.
beats.visual: diagram illustrating an accretion disk launching relativistic jets, 2011

beats.text: That relativistic jet crossed 3.8 billion light-years with its narrow beam aimed directly toward Earth.

beats.text: This head-on alignment significantly amplified its brightness, generating extraordinarily luminous and long-lived X-ray emissions.
